section_summary: This section consists chiefly of Panama American and El Panamá América clippings enclosed with a June 1933 American Legation despatch. The papers debate allegations that Japanese residents in Panama were evading taxes, undercutting local businesses, and spying on Canal defenses; they also print satire and rebuttals. The final clippings describe the arrival of the Japanese cruisers Iwate and Yakumo at Balboa and the official ceremonies surrounding their visit.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing
subfiles.about: A satirical column discusses Japanese residents and divided responsibility for Canal security.
subfiles.summary: Rounsevell presents his fictional adviser Barrister Sundown's explanations of why Army and Canal Zone officials allegedly do not monitor Japanese barbers, fishermen, and merchants.

subfiles.title: A Free Advertisement for Jap Light Globes
subfiles.about: A reader alleges Japanese espionage and unfair pricing of Japanese electric bulbs.
subfiles.summary: The letter calls for higher Panamanian duties on Japanese imports.

subfiles.title: Why the Jap Secrecy?
subfiles.about: Lung portrays the Japanese community's private gatherings as evidence of espionage.
subfiles.summary: The article contrasts Japanese residents with Chinese residents, alleging that Japanese merchants, barbers, and fishermen keep their meetings secret because they are part of a spy network.

subfiles.title: Japanese Spokesman No. 1
subfiles.about: A pseudonymous writer mocks Rounsevell's campaign against Japanese residents.
subfiles.summary: The letter jokes about tax evasion, Japanese barbers and shirtmakers, and a supposed coded message to Fort Randolph.

subfiles.title: Speakers Hit Japs Actions in Manchuria
subfiles.about: May Day speakers condemn Japanese actions in Manchuria and American influence in Panama.
subfiles.summary: The report covers labor demonstrations and a Communist Party manifesto.

subfiles.title: El dumping japonés en Panamá
subfiles.about: An editorial alleges that Japanese retail pricing harms Panamanian merchants and customs revenue.
subfiles.summary: The editorial sets aside the espionage claims to argue that Japanese firms receive state support, undersell local shops, pay low wages, and reduce import-tax receipts.

subfiles.title: Japanese Consul Will Entertain Officials Here
subfiles.about: The Japanese consul plans a dinner for Vice Admiral Hyakutake.
subfiles.summary: The notice also reports funds raised by the Japanese colony for the visiting ships.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: Second of May
subfiles.about: A satirical letter mocks Rounsevell's spy allegations and Canal military intelligence.
subfiles.summary: Its invented cables discuss Japanese barbers, fishermen, fortifications, and the columnist's suspicions.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: Third of May and Rounsevell's Reply
subfiles.doc_type: newspaper clipping; satirical letter and column
subfiles.from: Japanese in Rumble Seat; Nelson Rounsevell
subfiles.about: A satirical letter is followed by Rounsevell's emphatic reply about alleged Japanese espionage.
subfiles.summary: The pseudonymous writer jokes about official visits, intelligence, and the impending cruiser visit. Rounsevell responds that Japanese residents lack visible means of support, claims to have seen War Department documents at Casa Japonesa, and warns that saboteurs could destroy Canal facilities.

subfiles.title: Panamanian Interest in Japanese Menace
subfiles.about: A Panamanian reader urges attention to Rounsevell's warnings about the Canal.
subfiles.summary: The writer argues that damage to the locks would endanger Panama as well as the United States.

subfiles.title: 120 Japanese in Panama Have Failed to Register
subfiles.doc_type: newspaper clipping; article and name list
subfiles.about: Lung publishes names of Japanese residents he alleges have not registered.
subfiles.summary: The article accuses more than 120 Japanese residents of lacking required residence certificates and prints a two-page list of names. It calls for a government investigation of their status and motives.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: Japanese Sale
subfiles.about: A long satirical letter mocks espionage claims and names many local figures.
subfiles.summary: The writer imagines a Casa Japonesa sale of spy glasses, cameras, maps, and military goods, then extends a long list of absurd predictions involving Panama and Canal Zone residents.

subfiles.title: Two Japanese Give Proof of Registration
subfiles.doc_type: newspaper clipping; article with reproduced letter
subfiles.about: Casa Japonesa challenges the paper's claim that its employees were unregistered.
subfiles.summary: Sadairo sends residence certificates and asks the paper to correct its list.

subfiles.title: Jap Barbers Evade Taxes, Smash Efforts to Form Union
subfiles.about: Lung alleges Japanese barbers blocked a union and avoided municipal tax.
subfiles.summary: The article says officials plan to enforce a monthly barber tax.

subfiles.title: Jap Cruisers Due Saturday
subfiles.about: The paper previews Japanese cruisers' Balboa visit and other warship calls.
subfiles.summary: It identifies Iwate and Yakumo, their commanders, itinerary, and expected local hosts.

subfiles.title: Japanese in Rumble Seat: NR Admits It's Knocked Him Flat
subfiles.about: A headline refers to the Rumble Seat satire and Rounsevell.
subfiles.summary: Only the headline is legible in the supplied OCR.

subfiles.title: An American in the Driver's Seat
subfiles.from: An American in the Driver's Seat
subfiles.about: A reader urges military authorities to investigate Japanese activities near the Canal.
subfiles.summary: The writer supports Rounsevell's warnings and criticizes Quarry Heights and Panamanian officials for alleged inaction.

subfiles.title: President Arias on the Japanese Menace
subfiles.about: Panama's president comments on allegations of Japanese espionage.
subfiles.summary: Arias says his government has not yet assessed the claims but would act on clear evidence.

subfiles.title: Charges Japanese Merchants Exploit Native Laborers
subfiles.about: Lung alleges Japanese merchants pay Panamanian workers below the legal minimum.
subfiles.summary: The article links low wages and allegedly subsidized imports to unfair competition.

subfiles.title: Safety of Canal Not N.R.'s Business
subfiles.about: A reader disputes Rounsevell's alarm about Japanese residents.
subfiles.summary: Sackas expresses confidence in Quarry Heights and suggests prejudice is driving the campaign.

subfiles.title: Rumble Seat Letter of May Seventh
subfiles.about: A satirical writer jokes about intelligence searches and the arriving cruisers.
subfiles.summary: The letter names numerous local figures and imagines shipboard inspections, barber contests, and spying at Canal sites.

subfiles.title: Residents of Taboga Relate Visits of Jap Photographers
subfiles.about: Taboga residents allege Japanese visitors photographed Canal defenses.
subfiles.summary: The report says a warning to Fort Amador drew little interest and notes subsequent gun placements on Taboga.

subfiles.title: Rumble Seat Letter of Eighth May
subfiles.about: The satirical writer responds to J. Sackas and mocks Rounsevell's accusations.
subfiles.summary: The letter invites Rounsevell to meet the supposed spies and ends with a threatening comic verse.

subfiles.title: Rumble Seat Letter of Ninth May
subfiles.about: A satirical letter imagines officials hunting for the Rumble Seat writer.
subfiles.summary: It strings together jokes about local officials, police, intelligence, and Canal Zone installations.

subfiles.title: Rambling, Gambling and Publishing: Japanese Naval Visit
subfiles.about: Rounsevell warns readers to treat the Japanese cruiser visit as a security concern.
subfiles.summary: He portrays Japanese patriotism and self-sacrifice as reasons to fear sabotage, repeats allegations about resident barbers, fishermen, and shirtmakers, and calls for vigilance around Canal infrastructure. The column also cites a magazine story about alleged piloted bombs.

subfiles.title: Two Japanese Cruisers, 1,500 Officers and Men to Arrive
subfiles.about: The paper gives the schedule for Iwate and Yakumo's Balboa visit.
subfiles.summary: The article lists salutes, official calls, banquets, military reviews, a Canal transit for cadets, and visits to naval facilities. It names Japanese, American, and Panamanian hosts and officials.

subfiles.title: Two Japanese Navy Vessels Arrive Today
subfiles.about: The article explains the naval greetings and official calls planned for the cruisers' arrival.
subfiles.summary: It details salutes, rank protocol, the consul's reception, and Lieutenant Erdman's role as aide.

subfiles.title: Visiting Japanese Admiral Greeted by Zone, Army, Navy and Panama Officials
subfiles.about: The paper reports the cruisers' arrival and the first day's ceremonies.
subfiles.summary: Japanese residents greet the ships at Balboa, the crews exchange national anthems, and Hyakutake trades visits with American and Panamanian officials. A missed appointment with General Brown and a Union Club banquet are also reported.

subfiles.title: Fue imponente el saludo de los cadetes japoneses a las banderas de Panamá y Estados Unidos
subfiles.about: A Spanish-language report recounts the Japanese cruisers' Balboa welcome and official visits.
subfiles.summary: It describes the dockside reception, exchange of anthems, visits among Hyakutake and local officials, Brown's missed meeting, and the consul's banquet.
